modal_consistency_requirements.description: All modal components must follow consistent patterns and structure

requirements.rule: Always check existing modals before creating new ones
requirements.details: Search for existing modal components to understand the established patterns, naming conventions, and structure

requirements.rule: Use FormModalOrganism for all form-based modals
requirements.details: All modals that contain forms should use the FormModalOrganism component with consistent props structure
All modals should have: isOpen, onClose, onSubmit, and optional editingItem props with consistent naming
Use useState with form object, useEffect for editing mode, and consistent form reset patterns

requirements.rule: Always use Tailwind CSS, not standard CSS unless absolutely necessary
requirements.details: Always use Tailwind CSS, not standard CSS unless absolutely necessary
Use grid layouts for multiple fields, single divs for single fields, consistent spacing with space-y-4
Required fields should be marked, form validation in handleSubmit, reset form on success
All modals use a fixed size (450px height, max-w-lg width). No size prop needed. Content automatically scrolls if too long.
Use setForm(prev => ({ ...prev, [field]: value })) pattern for all field updates

All modals are automatically centered with fixed dimensions (450px height, max-w-lg width). Content automatically scrolls if it exceeds the modal height. Proper padding prevents content from being cut off at edges.

requirements.rule: Check for already existing components before creating new ones
requirements.details: Before creating a new component always check whats already there and if possible create a new component by combining existing components. This all comes down to using the atomic design pattern. I something is going to include a button use the Button.atom component for it and dont use html tags or create a new button component
Always follow the atomic design principles to keep component reusable and maintainable. This means splitting up components and using components that already exist to keep everything consistent.

ui_consistency_requirements.description: All pages and components must follow consistent UI patterns across the application

requirements.details:
When creating new pages or components, always check existing pages to match the UI styling. Page headers should use:
TitleDescription
Use default button size (not 'sm') for primary actions in cards and lists. Only use 'sm' size for secondary actions in tight spaces or inline elements.

requirements.rule: Check existing pages before creating new ones
requirements.details: Before creating a new page, search for similar pages in the same section (e.g., admin pages) to understand and match the established patterns, layouts, and styling conventions.
Use consistent spacing patterns: max-w-7xl for page containers, p-6 for page padding, space-y-6 for section spacing, and sm:flex patterns for responsive layouts.
Always use TextAtom component with consistent variants: 'h1' with weight='semibold' for page titles, 'small' with color='muted' for descriptions, and appropriate variants for other text elements.

database_migration_rules.description: Critical rules for handling database migrations safely

rules.details: Never use 'prisma migrate reset' as it will drop the entire database and lose all data. This is strictly forbidden in production environments.

rules.rule: Handle schema drift with db push for development
rules.details: When encountering schema drift, use 'prisma db push' to sync the schema without creating migration files, or resolve drift manually.

rules.rule: Use baseline migrations for existing databases
rules.details: For existing databases with data, use 'prisma migrate resolve --applied' to mark migrations as applied without running them.

rules.rule: Always backup before major schema changes
rules.details: Create database backups before making significant schema changes, especially in production.

rules.rule: Test migrations on development data first
rules.details: Always test schema changes on development environment with real data before applying to production.
